question: ‘Do or die’ slogan is given by which of the following freedom fighter?
solution:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi is associated with the maxim "do or die."**
 
• **During the Gandhiji-led Quit India Campaign, **this catchphrase was created.
 
• On August 9, 1942, **the Indian National Congress (INC),** under the direction of **Mahatma Gandhi**, formally introduced the catchphrase.
 
• **Its catchphrases were "Quit India" and "Bharat Chodo."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
 
• **​At Ratnagiri, Maharashtra, on July 23, 1856, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born.**
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a lawyer and freedom fighter**, is also known by the name** Lokmanya Tilak**.
 
• **"Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it," is the slogan.**
 
 
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**
 
 
• **First Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India from 1947 to 1950**, **Vallabhbhai Jhaverbhai Pate**l (31 October 1875 – 15 December 1950), also known as **Sardar Patel**, was an Indian lawyer, prominent political leader, barrister, and statesman.
 
• He was a lawyer and a prominent member of the **Indian National Congress **who** led the country's independence movement **and oversaw its fusion into a single, sovereign state.
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru**, a member of the **Indian National Congress,** was an Indian lawyer, activist, and politician who lived from 6 May 1861 to 6 February 1931. Also, he presided over Congress twice (1919–1920 and 1928–1929).
 
• **He was the ancestor of the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty** and the father of **India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.**
